clue.text: Face complaint about major road block

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the complaint is wrapped round the road

parts.note: a stye is an eye complaint, an inflamed swelling on the eyelid
the M1 is Britain's principal motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone moans about the roadblocks on a big motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb about confronting a complaint; it simply joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, just as to block someone's progress.

clue.text: One religious teacher keeled over after eating egg and cheese

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the egg goes inside the reversed letters
something that has keeled over has toppled, so these letters run in reverse order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a mullah is a Muslim teacher of religious law
an egg is O-shaped, a common crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: A mullah collapses after his breakfast of egg and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeled over' acts on both One and the teacher together, and the egg is swallowed by the reversed result.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloumi is a firm Cypriot cheese often eaten grilled.

clue.text: Batteries available with promotion in Riviera resort

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the resort's name

parts.note: Cannes is a resort on the French Riviera
on means available, as in 'the offer is on'
an ad is a promotion or advertisement

explanation.surface: Batteries are on special offer in a shop in Cannes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests electrical batteries; the definition means artillery batteries firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonade is a sustained bombardment from artillery batteries.

clue.text: Stare at search engine when out of work

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the work leaves the search engine's name

parts.note: Google is the best-known internet search engine
go means work or function, as in 'the engine won't go'

explanation.surface: Someone unemployed sits staring at a search engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to gaze at someone lecherously.

clue.text: Mutant regent's nip is showing

indicators.note: a mutant has changed form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mutated nip from the regent is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenting a thing is displaying or exhibiting it.

clue.text: Aged hero oddly doing headstand to see the moon

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing on its head turns the letters upside down, so they read in reverse
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the words

explanation.surface: An elderly hero does a headstand so as to view the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'Aged hero' are AEHR; flipped, they read upward to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the second-largest satellite of Saturn.

clue.text: Naughty Mexican casts adults-only flicks

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so these letters are reworked into a new order
casts means throws off, so a letter is discarded from the fodder

parts.note: X was the old British film certificate for adults only

explanation.surface: A mischievous Mexican stars in X-rated films.
explanation.walkthrough: MEXICAN loses its X and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is a casual term for the pictures, a picture house.

clue.text: Subtlety is introduced? That's a pest

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so is goes inside the subtlety

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that nuance introduced into a discussion is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoying person or thing, a pest in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Sailor prodded by Rear Admiral waving flag in battle

indicators.note: prodded by means poked into, so the following letters enter the sailor

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: a waving flag flutters, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor is jabbed by an admiral signalling with a flag in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' rearranges only the flag; the Rear Admiral's letters stay in order before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar was Nelson's 1805 naval victory over the French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: The sound of humming bird's call in verse form

indicators.note: the sound of means the words are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelly; high meat smells too; coo is the call of a dove or pigeon

explanation.surface: A hummingbird's call sounds in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming bird' reads as the tiny bird, but humming here means smelling bad, which is HIGH; HIGH COO said aloud gives the poem form.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese poem of three lines with seventeen syllables.

clue.text: The writer joins Jessica in 7 for a medley

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, who is me
7 is CINEMA: Jessica Lange is a film actress

explanation.surface: A writer teams up with Jessica at the cinema for a mixed programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 7 means cinema, where Jessica Lange made her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or assortment of varied things.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers, parsecs away

indicators.note: away means displaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Space travellers are parsecs from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacers are, in science fiction, people who journey through outer space over vast distances.

clue.text: One can't fly through the multiverse

indicators.note: through means the answer runs within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone flightless travels through the multiverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: African state without capital goes into negative profit sometimes

indicators.note: goes into means is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: no gain is a zero profit

indicators.note: without capital means losing its first letter

parts.note: Rwanda is a country in central Africa

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped African country sometimes ends up making a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' is read as losing its first letter, not as lacking money.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and again means occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Anglo-Irish Duke or Welsh Duke?

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: A question of whether a duke is Anglo-Irish or Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The second Duke is not a nobleman at all but the jazz great Duke Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, first Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo, was born in Dublin into the Anglo-Irish aristocracy.

clue.text: Training of son matters for 11

definitions.note: 11 refers to the answer MELANGE, a medley

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son's training covers a medley of subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a mixed collection, the same as a medley or mixture.

clue.text: Finally upgraded craft association

indicators.note: the final letter is raised a grade, as an exam mark E goes up to D

parts.note: guile is craft in the sense of cunning

explanation.surface: A craft association has at last been improved.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter E of GUILE is upgraded, as an exam grade, to D.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is a medieval association of craftsmen or merchants.

clue.text: Girl at function in charge of lots of stars

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
act means function or operate

explanation.surface: A girl at a party is in charge of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a party; here it is the verb meaning operate.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic means relating to a galaxy, a vast system of stars.

clue.text: Ready for trip to Transylvania and even parts of Algeria

indicators.note: even parts means the letters in even-numbered positions

explanation.surface: A traveller is ready for trips to Romania and Algeria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is the noun meaning cash, not the adjective; Transylvania is in Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: Lei are Romanian currency, money a traveller to Transylvania would need.

clue.text: Add excitement to long films having switched endings

indicators.note: the two end letters swap places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: epics are long films on a grand scale

explanation.surface: A director adds thrills to long films by changing their endings.
explanation.walkthrough: EPICS with its first and last letters swapped, E and S, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spice something up is to make it more lively or exciting.

clue.text: Formation of concepts in countryside at Iona

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Ideas form in the countryside at Iona.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideation is the mental process of forming ideas.

clue.text: Garden fly is flying around plant

indicators.note: flying around suggests chaotic movement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A garden fly buzzes around a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's finger is a name for okra and for kidney vetch, both plants.

clue.text: Dancer strangled debt collector with abandon

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of debts
to can is to scrap or abandon a plan

explanation.surface: A dancer throttled a bailiff in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with abandon' sounds like wildness; abandon is the verb meaning give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan, the modern-dance pioneer, died when her scarf caught in a car wheel and choked her.

clue.text: Desert area, say, without river

indicators.note: without means outside, so the abbreviation goes round the river

parts.note: say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: A desert region, for instance, lacking a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An erg is a large sea of sand dunes in the Sahara.

clue.text: See 26
Former PM caught knocking prince out

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out means removed, so the prince leaves the word

parts.note: knocking means criticising, panning

explanation.surface: A former prime minister was caught punching a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out' looks like a punch; knocking is criticising, PANNING, with P taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: George Canning was briefly British prime minister in 1827.

clue.text: It's said the composer has a hospital trolley — this composer

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: the composer is the setter, so this is 'I've a', said aloud
a gurney is a wheeled stretcher used in hospitals

explanation.surface: Apparently the composer owns a hospital trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The composer' at first means a musician, but it is the puzzle's composer speaking: 'I've a' sounds like IVOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Gurney was an English poet and songwriter of the First World War era.

clue.text: What measures I encountered when diving into a foreign sea

indicators.note: diving into means plunging inside, so this goes within the sea

parts.note: mer is French for sea
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone describes meeting something while diving into a sea abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument that measures electric current, conventionally written I.

clue.text: A journey almost entirely without water

indicators.note: almost entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A journey that is nearly all without water.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is dry, receiving almost no rainfall.

clue.text: A husband breaks vow in church state

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the letters go inside the vow

parts.note: I do is the vow made at a church wedding

explanation.surface: A husband breaks his wedding vow in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the northwestern United States.

clue.text: Byzantine church feature with two heads

definitions.text: Byzantine church feature with two heads

parts.words: Byzantine church feature with two heads
parts.note: the feature is described as two slang words for a person's head joined together

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the answer are slang for a head, so the feature literally has two heads.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion dome is a bulbous cupola typical of Russian Orthodox and Byzantine-style churches.
